{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZhJBfw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDIKQQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 55, "title": "Correct V30MZ flags after successful AAM and AAD", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `296ab20178ce8228581f64ea385d8b472b32b4fb`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:942–959` updates only SZP after AAM/AAD. Successful AAM therefore retains incoming AF/CF/OF; AAD omits the final addition’s AF/CF/OF. Software branching on those flags can take incorrect paths. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

Static reproductions, not executed during planning:

| Instruction | Input | Current result | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AAM `0A` | AL=`2A`, FLAGS=`F8D7` | AX=`0402`, FLAGS=`F813` | AX=`0402`, FLAGS=`F002` |
| AAD `0A` | AX=`0106`, FLAGS=`F002` | AX=`0010`, FLAGS=`F002` | AX=`0010`, FLAGS=`F012` |

The existing `decimal_conversion_flags_and_extended_string_comparisons` test checks conversion results without asserting their complete flags.

## Expected outcome

Successful AAM with a nonzero immediate base clears AF/CF/OF and derives SZP from remainder AL. AAD truncates `AH × base` to eight bits, adds original AL, clears AH, and sets all six arithmetic flags from that final byte addition. Preserve control/fixed flag bits and unrelated architectural state.

Apply these semantics across emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations. Limit production changes to successful conversions and necessary tests, original fixtures, browser integration and documentation. Preserve existing zero-base AAM fault behavior; disputed exceptional semantics remain separate work.

## Context

The clean checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; all 54 closed-work titles were inspected without finding equivalent completed work. Earlier arithmetic milestones remain regression obligations.

The pinned [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) describes instruction-specific successful-conversion flags. Its [AAD calculator](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L5007) uses byte ADD after modulo-256 product accumulation; its [AAM experiment](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L5920) compares full FLAGS under contrasting inputs. These are inspected experiment sources, without independently inspected per-model silicon logs. Applying the shared CPU rules across graphics modes is an instruction-level inference.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), §§1.3 and 3.1.5, distinguishes conversion immediate-byte behavior and defines ordinary byte-add flags. It does not independently establish every console-specific conversion flag. The experiment’s `F202` includes its incoming IF and must not become an unconditional emulator constant. AAM fault-ZF prose contradicts its calculator, so that uncertainty does not govern this successful-conversion correction.

Correction record: replace the existing assumption that SZP-only updates suffice with the two instruction-specific rules above. Record the old assumption, corrected requirement, sources and rationale. Evidence-based corrections require neither human approval nor independent AI re-review; preserve the agreed goal and relevant acceptance.

[Saved #53 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/296ab20178ce8228581f64ea385d8b472b32b4fb/docs/issue-53-validation.md) reports 149 core unit tests, 27 integration tests, one adapter test and complete production Chromium suites passing. These are reported results, not planning-time executions. That record still requests final Coordinator review; it does not establish conversion correctness or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Correct successful AAM/AAD through ordinary decoding. Preserve two-byte consumption, continuation, unrelated registers/segments, control/fixed flags, existing execution components, mapped fetch accounting and zero-base AAM fault handling. Avoid unrelated arithmetic or scheduler changes.
- [ ] Add independently derived literal AX/full-FLAGS vectors, including both reproductions above and contrasting incoming arithmetic flags. Cover AAM bases `1,2,10,16,255`, ignored incoming AH, zero/nonzero quotient and remainder, and remainder sign/parity boundaries. Cover AAD bases `0,1,10,16,128,255`, product truncation, addition carry, auxiliary carry, signed overflow, zero, sign and parity. Expected values must not call production conversion/ALU helpers.
- [ ] Exercise emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, supported graphics modes and Color/Crystal runtime mode round trips. Assert instruction continuation and flag-dependent branches. Retain zero-base fault, multiplication, division, shift/rotate, PUSH SP, prefix and interrupt regressions; verify normal Machine scheduling still advances shared devices using unchanged accounting.
- [ ] Add or extend an original source-included CC0 cartridge using `fixtures/build.py` and NASM. Native and production Chromium/Wasm checks must compare actual CPU-written conversion results, full FLAGS and branch observations against independent literals on every model and fresh restart. Include supported Color/Crystal mode transitions, clear volatile observations and invalidate poisoned retained success records. Record focused baseline native and cartridge failures, configurations reached, and corrected passes.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator passes `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`. In `web`, pass `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview.
- [ ] Preserve existing three-model, startup/firmware, video/input/frame, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, RTC transport, SRAM/EEPROM, Wasm/browser lifecycle and save-integrity acceptance. Preserve ROM identity, browser-local ownership/persistence and provenance policies; require no proprietary ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Update `docs/hardware-subset.md`, source reconciliation and fixture/provenance documentation. Record actual commands, failures, resolutions, passes and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox before merge, distinguishing tests present from reported passes and leaving unresolved hardware/commercial coverage explicit.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-browser discrimination, additional browser engines and additional lawfully available software. Physical-console comparisons and human gameplay are optional evidence, unperformed during planning; neither is a merge prerequisite. No application builds or tests were run during planning.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
